newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-VIDIRI DAZZLES AS BARBARIANS ROUT NORTH.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-VIDIRI DAZZLES AS BARBARIANS ROUT NORTH.

text.p: Speedy Fijian Joeli Vidiri gave a dazzling display as the New Zealand Barbarians rugby union touring team crushed the North 86-0 on Sunday.

Vidiri made a spectacular entry as a tactical second-half substitute in the 14-try rout over a hastily-assembled, patched-up North side with borrowed tracksuits who trained together for the first time on Saturday.

Vidiri, who will not be eligible for the All Blacks until 1998 after switching his allegiance from Fiji, put Carlos Spencer over for a try with his first touch and then raced over for a hat-trick of tries as the touring team cut loose.
The biggest obstacle to the Barbarians came in the form of a heavy snow shower that produced tricky conditions under foot.
However, the weather did not dampen the enthusiasm of Jonah Lomu, who adopted a roaming role, popping up on both wings in addition to driving down the middle.
The winger knocked on with his first touch of the ball but delighted the crowd with his storming runs, which invariably took a minimum of three defenders to pull him down.
There were first-half tries for flankers Andrew Blowers (two) and Dylan Mika, prop Olo Brown, number eight Taine Randell and full-back Chris Cullen.
Leading 40-0 at the break, the Barbarians continued the one-way traffic with Viri registering his hat-trick and other tries coming from Spencer (two), Robin Brooke and Mark Robinson.
Spencer also kicked seven goals from nine attempts for a personal points tally of 24.
